findings.claim: The no-link decision treats G_{F,S} as only local-Galois/cohomological work and omits the finite global arithmetic needed to construct its maximal restricted-ramification extension. The finite extensions unramified away from S must be closed under compositum, exactly the NFA1.5 input already routed to IntegralIwasawaTheory L1 for the analogous construction. Neither an edge nor an indirect path to R02.3 records this input.
findings.evidence: content/tau-ceti/NumberFieldArithmetic/README.md:607, section 1.5: '`p` unramified in `L₁` and in `L₂` implies `p` unramified in `L₁L₂`.' content/campaign/ArithmeticGaloisDuality/README.md:48, R02.3: 'Define G_{F,S}, including the archimedean and p-adic places demanded by the theorem.' Taking the maximal extension unramified outside S requires the finite-compositum closure before the union and Krull-topological quotient; this is independent of the local cohomology conditions. The partial unreviewed ArithmeticGaloisDuality packet's NFA1 request and restricted-ramification-group node corroborate the reading but are not its authority. The target's own IntegralIwasawaTheory:L1 link already recognizes this finite/infinite boundary. At revision 1e05797cdde7eddde576b7cf74a8d705644a978f the actual assembled graph and other research link packets contain no supplier route; no reverse path prevents adding it.
findings.fix: Add an inferred two-sided-evidence link NFA Layer 1 -> ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3 and correct the examined entry. Quote the compositum law and R02.3's G_{F,S} construction. Do not claim NFA supplies an infinite Galois group. The proposed pair passes the link validator and acyclic merge in the scratch check.

findings.claim: The no-link decision overlooks an accepted integrated consumer of the NFA discriminant/different outputs. The Faltings decomposition explicitly needs a discriminant bound with wild ramification allowed in S before applying bounded-discriminant finiteness, yet NFA4 and NFA6 have no route to its R28.1 parent or Hermite-Minkowski node. Its existing gap identifies the missing assembly; the link map should route the already-owned inputs without pretending that they prove the full restricted-ramification finiteness theorem.
findings.evidence: data/decompositions/FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems.json:308-320, independently accepted node R28.1/hermite-minkowski-finiteness-of-extensions-unramified-outside-S: 'bound the discriminant d_{K'/Q} in terms of [K' : Q] and S using the different and the ramification filtration, then apply the Hermite-Minkowski finiteness theorem for number fields of bounded discriminant.' Its hypotheses explicitly allow wild ramification in S; its gap at line 1744 calls for the missing different bound. Its link to the bounded-height finiteness node records the descent use. The authoritative R28.1 README:28 says 'Prove the descent and level-structure arguments needed to convert moduli points into isomorphism classes.' NFA README:1139 states 'relDiscr A C = (relDiscr A B) ^ [M : L] · Ideal.relNorm A (relDiscr B C).' NFA6.4, lines 1817-1818, states '`e ≤ v_P(𝔡) ≤ e − 1 + v_P(e)` when it is wildly ramified, with `v_P(e)` the multiplicity of `P` in `span {(e : 𝓞 L)}`.' NFA5.10 supplies the residue-degree-weighted assembly. Mathlib at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Basic.lean:496-499, NumberField.finite_of_discr_bdd, actually assumes the discriminant bound. Tau Ceti at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Discriminant/Separable.lean:50, already has relDiscr_tower. Neither proposed pair has a forward or reverse path in the actual assembled atlas.
